mechanism: Amphotericin B causes nephrotoxicity and electrolyte depletion (hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia) which can potentiate anticholinergic effects and cardiac arrhythmias; scopolamine's anticholinergic properties may mask symptoms of amphotericin B toxicity.
action: Monitor serum electrolytes closely, assess cardiac function, limit scopolamine use to essential indications only, and consider alternative antiemetics with lower anticholinergic burden.
